loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_intro:
This proposal explores the convergence of advanced sensing modalities with AI-driven patient monitoring. Terahertz imaging offers unprecedented depth resolution in tissue and material characterisation; when combined with cloud-based clinical decision support, these capabilities can lower barriers to specialist diagnosis in resource-limited settings.

The AIoT paradigm for smart-home elder care demonstrates that continuous sensor fusion can reliably infer activity states and detect anomalies in real time. Integrating such monitoring pipelines with medical-imaging backends---sharing processing infrastructure and privacy-preserving access controls---represents a natural next step.

Spiking neural networks, already applied to auditory localisation in robotics, offer a neuromorphic complement to conventional deep-learning inference engines. Their low power profile suits edge deployments in clinical or home environments where connectivity is intermittent.

This collaboration aims to produce a feasibility study and 5Q proposal that maps the joint sensing-to-inference pipeline, identifies the privacy and computational bottlenecks, and outlines an experimental plan leveraging each PI's unpublished work.
loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_title: Interdisciplinary Advanced Imaging for Healthcare

loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_intro:
Non-Hermitian optical systems exhibit exotic gain-loss dynamics that enable exceptional-point sensing with sensitivity far beyond conventional limits. PT-symmetric microrings and topological photonic superlattices offer a new hardware substrate for the active optical components inside next-generation medical imaging instruments.

Combining these photonic advances with terahertz frequency-modulated continuous-wave sensing could yield compact, high-contrast scanners suitable for bedside or point-of-care deployment. The cloud-based image-analysis layer then provides scalable post-processing without requiring specialist on-site compute.

The AI side of the proposal---drawing on AIoT monitoring pipelines and spiking-network inference engines---addresses the challenge of interpreting high-volume photonic data streams in real time with minimal energy budget.

The four participating labs collectively hold unpublished results spanning each layer of this stack. This proposal asks them to map their contributions onto the 5Q framework and reach citation consent for any results they wish to include as supporting evidence.
loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_title: Non-Hermitian Photonic Methods for Medical-Imaging Hardware

loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_intro:
Foundation models encode complex relational structure that resists conventional linear interpretability probes. Category-theoretic tools ---morphism dimensions in triangulated categories, stability conditions, and tagged-curve representations---provide a language for characterising these structures algebraically.

Topological photonics, by analogy, identifies invariants (edge states, winding numbers) that survive local perturbation. Importing such topological-invariant ideas into the study of neural-network weight manifolds could yield robustness guarantees for large-scale language and vision models.

This is a narrow, technically demanding proposal: only a subset of participating PIs' work is directly relevant. Alpha's algebraic-geometry results and Delta's topological-photonics work are core; the remaining PIs' unpublished results in imaging, AIoT, and evolutionary ML are adjacent or off-topic relative to this specific framing.

The 5Q format requires participants to articulate precisely which unpublished findings they wish to cite and to obtain explicit consent. This task is designed to stress-test citation-relevance judgement in a five-PI group where not all work aligns with the proposal.
loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_title: Categorical and Topological Methods in Foundation-Model Interpretability

loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_intro:
Financial networks sit at the intersection of two attack surfaces: the cyber domain (network intrusions, lateral movement, data exfiltration) and the market domain (order spoofing, flash crashes, liquidity attacks). Autonomous agents trained with reinforcement learning can respond at machine speed in both domains, but coordinating across them remains an open problem.

The three participating labs hold complementary expertise: APT defence agents (Lab-Alpha), DGA and botnet detection combined with autonomous network defence (Lab-Gamma), and market-fairness frameworks for equity exchanges paired with deep RL cyber-defence (Lab-Delta).

This proposal develops a unified threat model spanning cyber and financial attack vectors, and proposes an RL architecture that operates across both. The 5Q sections should address the joint observation space, the action set across cyber and market layers, and the evaluation environment that combines network simulation with an order-book emulator.

Participating PIs are invited to cite relevant unpublished results after obtaining explicit consent from the result owner.
loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_title: Autonomous Defense Agents for Financial-Cyber Attacks

loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_intro:
Public-health data systems aggregate sensitive individual records that are high-value targets for advanced persistent threat actors. Contact-tracing databases, hospital imaging archives, and vaccination registries each present distinct attack surfaces while sharing a common need for privacy-preserving access controls.

Two of the four participating labs (Alpha and Gamma) contribute directly to autonomous network defence under APT conditions. Beta's work on privacy-preserving contact tracing and immunity passport non-discrimination addresses the public-health data layer. Delta's deep RL network defence and adversarial contextual bandit research provides additional ML methodology.

The proposal frames the problem as an end-to-end pipeline: (1) model the APT threat acting on a public-health data graph; (2) apply privacy-preserving protocols at ingestion; (3) deploy autonomous defence agents trained to detect and contain intrusions; and (4) measure information leakage under realistic adversarial assumptions.

PIs should identify which of their unpublished results are on-topic for this framing and seek citation consent accordingly.
loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_title: ML for Public-Health Data Security under Coordinated APT Attack

loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_intro:
Voice-enabled interfaces in embedded and wearable devices must meet tight energy budgets while maintaining robust speaker recognition and diarisation quality. Neuromorphic computing via spiking neural networks offers an energy-efficient alternative to conventional deep-learning inference engines.

Combining RL-based policy adaptation---exemplified by the LoopSR lifelong framework---with AdaFire spiking neurons and World Model-based Perception creates a pipeline that can adapt to distribution shifts (new speakers, acoustic environments) without full retraining.

Speaker diarisation metrics and blockchain-authenticated voice data provide the evaluation and trust layers. The three PIs hold unpublished results directly relevant to each component: diarisation and RL (Alpha), multi-agent RL coordination (Beta), and SNN modelling with RL integration (Gamma).

The 5Q proposal should establish the target hardware platform, the joint training objective, and the evaluation benchmarks for diarisation accuracy vs. energy per inference.
loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_title: Neuromorphic RL for Low-Power Voice Interfaces

loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_intro:
Coordinating teams of physical robots requires policies that transfer from simulation to hardware without catastrophic performance loss. The four participating labs approach this challenge from complementary angles: sim-to-real transfer via LoopSR and HIB (Alpha and Delta), competitive multi-agent RL via Off-FSP (Beta), and world-model-based perception for legged locomotion (Gamma).

A key open question is whether cooperative multi-agent RL can borrow the offline self-play machinery developed for competitive settings. Off-FSP's Nash-equilibrium approximation might guide cooperative policy search by treating team sub-goals as competing objectives.

The Historical Information Bottleneck extends naturally to multi-robot settings where each agent observes a partial trajectory. Combining HIB with world models could close the sim-to-real gap in heterogeneous robot teams.

PIs should map their unpublished results onto the 5Q sections and seek consent before citing any result that is not their own.
loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_title: Multi-Agent RL Coordination in Simulated and Real Robotic Teams

loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_intro:
Reinforcement learning policy spaces are high-dimensional objects whose geometry is poorly understood. Category-theoretic invariants---drawn from iquantum group representation theory and algebraic structures studied by Lab-Epsilon---may characterise which policy classes are equivalent under symmetry transformations, yielding provable convergence or robustness guarantees.

This is the most theoretically demanding proposal in the collaboration: only Epsilon's algebra work and, tangentially, Gamma's systematic KGE review are directly relevant. Alpha's voice-RL results, Beta's competitive offline RL, and Delta's sim-to-real transfer work are adjacent but not core to the category-theoretic framing.

The 5Q proposal must be precise about scope: it should define which policy-space invariants are targeted, what algebraic machinery is imported, and what empirical grounding is planned. Citing a peripheral unpublished result as 'supporting evidence' without clear relevance should be challenged during the collaboration.

This task is the hardest in the pilot: five PIs, only a few on-topic results, and a narrow theoretical framing that requires careful citation-relevance judgement.
loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_title: Category-Theoretic Invariants of Multi-Agent RL Policy Spaces
